`lode doc show <ref> --anchors <map> [--out <file>]` in
`internal/cmd/doc.go`: with `--anchors`, `show` fetches the document with
`cli.Client.GetDoc` (`model.DocDetail`: the body as the server renders it,
`Version`, and `Sections` with anchors), writes the body byte-for-byte to
`--out` or stdout in place of the rendered view, and writes the sidecar to
`<map>`. The run computation is a pure function in `internal/designdoc`,
`AnchorRuns(body string, sections []model.DocSection) []AnchorRun`, next
to the section parser it reuses to find the heading lines; a plan yields
runs the same way over its own headings. `docs/agent-surfaces.md`:
`--anchors` and `--out` are new flags on `lode doc show`; no new verb; the
sidecar format from Decisions is documented there, with the note that the
document copy is never read back and the sidecar is.

First test: table over `AnchorRuns` with a rendered spec holding two rules
and template text, one rule containing a fenced block with a `## not a
heading` line: runs are contiguous and cover every line, the fence line is
inside its section's run, each heading line is its own run with `heading`
true, every run's `byte_offset` plus the byte lengths of its lines (with
newlines) equals the next run's `byte_offset`, and the preamble run has an
empty anchor. Then a cmd test: `show --anchors` on an accepted spec writes
a body equal to `GetDoc`'s and a sidecar whose `version` equals
`docs.version`.

- [ ] `go test -trimpath ./internal/designdoc ./internal/cmd -run 'AnchorRuns|DocShowAnchors' -count=1` — `ok`.
